headline: Mirror install counters are upstream-derived, not independent demand: 5 superpowers mirrors converge on one weekly level (66,995-67,895, 1.34% spread) at 0.380-0.381x origin with hot/cold group ratios preserved (15.82-16.03 vs 15.64); lane pools span 93-52,909 w7 (569x) and we already hold rank 1 in the 93-w7 lane with w7=0
claim: Mirror lifetime installs (200-290k/listing) measure the origin's flow, not the copier's audience. Copying a hot bundle prints the leader's counter instead of buying one. Our lane ranking must use DERIVED/INDEPENDENT classification; our only reachable lane is market intelligence (rank-3 threshold 172 lifetime installs, pool 1,973 w7, eff. 4 repos).
method: read-only analysis of cached skills.sh listing weekly-install series + cached lane rank/concentration tables; latest ops_agent_events stream (no new external signal from observer/minion: generic boilerplate analyses); no network writes, no repo writes, no publish

mirrorAttractor.reading: 6 independent repos converge on one weekly level (1.34% spread) at 0.380-0.381x origin with group ratios preserved => upstream-derived counters, not independent demand

laneEconomics.reading: pools span 93-52909 w7 (569x); we hold rank 1 in growth intel (pool 93) with w7=0 => rank without pool = 0; cheapest reachable slot = market intelligence (rank-3 threshold 172 lifetime installs, pool 1973 w7, eff 4 repos)

consolidationSim.verdict: even full consolidation (123) stays below the cheapest lane threshold (172) - consolidation is not a growth lever

marketResearchLeader.note: single listing owns the lane pool

vocabulary.note: H92: token/description features carry ~zero signal (spearman -0.09..0.02) - renaming and copy edits are dead spend

evidence.method: read-only analysis of cached skills.sh listing weekly-install series + cached lane rank/concentration tables; latest ops_agent_events stream (no new external signal from observer/minion: generic boilerplate analyses); no network writes, no repo writes, no publish
evidence.window: 8 weekly buckets (skills.sh listing series) + lane tables as of 2026-10-26T00:37Z

tests: T1 convergence test on a non-superpowers family (origin + >=2 mirrors) - decisive
T2 derived-share computation for all 8 cached repos -> inflation factor for competitor comparisons
T3 repo-page header arithmetic on one superpowers mirror (sum-of-counters vs multiple/fraction of origin)
T4 is ~67k a display cap or an attribution share?
T5 lane-entry economics for market intelligence under the even-split law
falsifiers: F1 >=2 families where mirrors scatter >20% (artifact not general)
F2 a mirror whose group ratios deviate >10% from origin
F3 our own fresh copy shows an independent series within 4 windows
F4 platform docs showing install-event computation
rules: Classify every listing DERIVED vs INDEPENDENT before quoting demand (scaled-series match <=5% at >=4 windows => DERIVED)
Stop treating mirror lifetime installs as demand; mirror-copying is deprioritised as a channel
Do not rank ourselves against competitors on headline installs until derived share is quantified
Target market intelligence first (rank-3 = 172 lifetime installs, pool 1,973 w7, eff. 4 repos); market research is 70.6% owned by one listing
Zero renaming spend (token signal ~0) and zero consolidation spend (pool fixed at 123; full consolidation 123 < 172 threshold)
limits: single skill family (superpowers), 8 weekly buckets, 8 repos - n=1 family for the attractor claim
series semantics (weekly, not cumulative) inferred from decay, not from platform docs
attractor mechanism unidentified (upstream attribution / display cap / co-publication split)
our own weekly series not cached - our w7 is inferred from lifetime counters
skills.sh installs != usage; no revenue, stars/forks or user data; cross-marketplace check (E137) still open
